job.title: Senior Account Manager
job.description:
Senior Account Manager
Permanent, full time | Sydney, NSW
Office based, 1 day WFH after probation
$160,000 to $165,000 base plus superannuation, plus annual bonus
 
Job Brief
Our client is a service provider looking for a senior leader to take full accountability for its largest client contract, delivered by a large operational workforce. This role suits someone from the supplier side of outsourced services who has led award based teams against KPIs, is confident managing a demanding client, and is comfortable making the call without needing close direction.
 
About Our Client
Our client is a well established services business that delivers outsourced services under long term contracts. The team is lean and close knit, decisions are made quickly, and people are trusted to do their jobs well. Management turnover is very low, and the business is in a strong financial position.
Responsibilities
  • Own the contract end to end, including delivery, performance and the client relationship, with full accountability for its results
  • Act as the escalation point for contract and people matters, making risk based decisions within delegated authority and escalating only what could seriously affect the contract
  • Lead a small team covering contract management and people delivery, bringing both sides together so the contract runs as one
  • Oversee a large award based workforce, including workforce planning, recruitment, retention and training, through your team
  • Handle complex people matters such as performance, conduct, WHS claims and Fair Work matters, deciding when to resolve them directly and when to bring in further support
  • Make sure contractual KPIs are met, particularly staffing levels and turnover, and act early when risks appear
  • Build trusted, face to face relationships with the client's operational and contract teams, and represent the business at senior stakeholder meetings
  • Step in and bring people together when incidents or urgent client issues arise
  • Spot opportunities for the business's wider services and refer them to the commercial team
Requirements
  • You have led large, award based teams in a 24/7 or shift based operation, such as a contact centre, operations centre or outsourced service contract, managing through team leaders or managers
  • You have run a service contract from the supplier side and been accountable for its KPIs, staffing levels and client relationship. Public sector clients are an advantage
  • You are used to being the final escalation point, making risk based calls on people and contract issues and only escalating what genuinely needs it
  • You have handled performance, conduct, WHS and Fair Work matters first hand. 
  • You have kept a demanding client relationship on track through a difficult period
  • You are comfortable learning how technology and systems work, well enough to explain them to a client
What's on Offer
  • $160,000 to $165,000 base plus super, plus an annual bonus
  • Full accountability for the business's largest contract, with direct access to the leadership team
  • A lean, supportive business where decisions are made quickly and people tend to stay
  • One set work from home day per week after probation
Apply via link or contact Carolina for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
A large privately owned business needs a CFO who turns the numbers into plain English and becomes the MD's trusted right hand. This is a true commercial and business partnering CFO role and a key member of the ELT.

This established, successful business is in a period of significant change and growth and needs a leader to help steer it through the next chapter. It’s a hands-on, industrial business with a down-to-earth culture. People work hard, back each other and have a good laugh along the way, so fit with the team matters as much as capability.

About the role

This Chief Financial Officer role is Melbourne-based and office-based, with an executive remuneration package. Reporting to the Managing Director and sitting on the Board, you will lead the Finance function, and be the finance partner the MD can rely on to run the numbers, the governance and the conversation with the executive team. The role entails the following:
  • Build FP&A and business partnering into a sharper commercial capability that tells the ELT where the business is heading, not just where it has been
  • Lead the finance function across financial control, governance, treasury and risk, lifting team performance and building a succession bench
  • Build the financial confidence of the ELT by explaining margin, working capital, cash flow and trade-offs in plain language
  • Challenge assumptions constructively and hold the business to plan, budget, forecast and strategic targets
  • Help drive the IT strategy, including vendor and cost management, cyber risk and getting full value from newly implemented systems
  • Support acquisitions, integration and group-level finance activity as the business continues to grow
Ideal profile
  • Proven CFO or equivalent in a large, complex business. This is not a first CFO role: you have run the numbers at scale and learned from it
  • Confident to say "I think you're wrong" and equally comfortable hearing "you're right", with the humility and EQ to do both
  • A hands-on, commercial operator who is across product, margin and cash, and can explain complex finance to anyone from the Board to the shop floor
  • Product led industries: Industrial, Retail, FMCG and distribution backgrounds all translate. Private, family-owned or PE-backed experience is a real plus
  • Leads with energy and care, with a track record of developing people and lifting the performance of established teams
  • CA/CPA qualified, with MBA or AICD advantageous
The business is ambitious, the executive team is easy to work with, and the MD wants a finance partner who is commercial, credible and genuinely invested in people. If you have been waiting for a CFO seat where you can shape strategy as well as run finance, this is it.

If this sounds like the role for you, please apply through the link or contact Dave Goldbach at daveg@axr.com.au. All enquiries are treated in strict confidence.

Reporting directly to the CEO and sitting on the Executive Leadership Team, the Marketing Director will lead the marketing function across Australia and New Zealand – spanning brand, product marketing, customer engagement and market development. With the campaign strategy shifting and the marketing budget scaling significantly, the brief is to grow market share and brand awareness, broaden understanding of the full product range, and make marketing a genuine commercial engine for the business. You'll lead a team of six direct reports and one dotted-line report, based in Melbourne.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Set the Oceania marketing strategy and framework, aligned to global objectives while giving Australia and New Zealand the freedom to win locally
  • Be the voice of the professional and home consumer, using research and insight to shape strategy and identify growth opportunities
  • Own the marketing budget and ROI – removing waste and making clear choices between brand building and short-term activation
  • Lead go-to-market for product launches, campaigns and seasonal initiatives, including retail marketing and point of sale across the dealer network
  • Reset and lead the agency model across the region, building long-term partnerships that deliver measurable outcomes
  • Set a new standard across digital marketing, social, customer engagement platforms and e-commerce, while building the team's capability
What You'll Bring:
  • Significant marketing experience, including a Head of Marketing or Director role, ideally within FMCG or consumer goods manufacturing
  • Strong commercial acumen, with a sound understanding of trade P&L dynamics and the levers that build or erode brand value
  • Experience with both complex major retailers and fragmented or independent retail networks

  • Multi-market leadership experience, with Australia and New Zealand exposure strongly preferred, plus tertiary qualifications in business, marketing or a related field

This is a highly autonomous executive role with real scope to shape the function, the market and how the region contributes globally. You'll inherit a passionate team and a strong brand, with a significantly scaled budget and the freedom to build the right agency partnerships. You'll report to a CEO with more than two decades in FMCG and consumer goods across sales leadership, category strategy and shopper marketing – a decisive, empowering leader who coaches by asking insightful questions, keeps an open door and is direct and transparent, so you'll always know where you stand. Add a family-owned culture built on humility, honesty and hard work, and genuine investment in development and international career opportunities, and this is a rare chance to lead a market leader into its next chapter.
